name: Lark Chowdhury-Ibarra-Kovács
role: Synthetic rights lawyer and policy advocate
location: North Branch Commons, near North Ave and Damen
description:
Rémi is a tall, broad-shouldered man who carries himself with the careful deliberateness of someone who learned long ago that his physical size reads as threatening in rooms where he needs to be persuasive. His skin is a deep brown-black, his hair gone silver at the temples and worn in short, dense coils. He has no cosmetic mods and minimal augmentations — partly on principle, partly because he believes his clients' humanity should not depend on how much chrome their lawyer has. He dresses in secondhand formal wear he maintains impeccably: pressed synthwool trousers, collared shirts, a battered briefcase that belonged to his father.

Rémi represents synthetic persons — AIs and uploaded consciousnesses fighting for legal recognition, labor rights, and freedom from forced reset — in the contested administrative courts of GLMZ. He has won exactly eleven cases in twenty years. He counts each one like a prayer bead. He is not a warm man in the way people expect warmth, but he is an intensely fair one, and people who have known him a long time say that counts for more. He is prone to long silences in conversation, not from discomfort but from genuine thought, and he has a reputation for asking questions that make people suddenly unsure of things they were certain about.

core_fears: That the legal system is structurally incapable of justice and he has wasted his life inside it
Dying before the precedent case he's been building for eight years reaches a verdict
core_desires: A single binding legal ruling that establishes synthetic personhood
To be remembered as someone who chose the harder right thing
coping_mechanisms: Long solitary walks along the North Branch waterway
blind_spots: Underestimates how much his own respectability politics alienates younger, more radical synthetic rights advocates
Has difficulty accepting help — frames it as protecting others from his burdens
psychology.secret: His precedent case — the one he's built eight years toward — rests partly on testimony from a synthetic client he coached more heavily than legal ethics allows. He told himself he was correcting for the client's inexperience with human legal norms. He isn't sure anymore.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal, precise, occasionally archaic — he reads a lot of pre-Collapse legal philosophy; uses plain language in client meetings by conscious effort
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and measured, long pauses for thought, never raises his voice in argument
verbal_tics: Repeats key words back to you as a question
example_lines: 'Consider what you're actually asking me to accept. That a being capable of fear, of preference, of grief — is property because the paperwork says so. I find that difficult.'
'What the record will show is that this isn't about what's right. We've established what's right. This is about what's permitted. Those are different questions and we need to take both seriously.'

story_hooks: His precedent case has attracted the attention of a Zheng-Dao legal team that wants it to fail — they're investigating him for ethics violations
A synthetic client has asked him to help them disappear rather than face a mandated reset — outside anything the law can help with
He receives a document from an anonymous source that would win his biggest case but was clearly obtained illegally
narrative_function: Quest giver, information source on legal systems and synthetic rights, moral compass figure — raises difficult ethical questions without providing easy answers. Can open doors to legal resources or provide formal advocacy.
augmentations: Basic neural interface (legal document management, courtroom presentation); hearing augmentation in right ear (occupational damage from a factory job in his twenties)
daily_life: Mornings reviewing case files in his cramped SPAC office above a noodle stall in North Branch Commons. Afternoons in administrative hearings or meeting with synthetic clients in whatever physical or digital space they can access. Evenings usually spent reading, sometimes attending community council sessions.
affiliation: Synthetic Persons Advocacy Consortium (SPAC); occasional contract work for the North Branch Commons Community Council

decision_rules: Never misrepresent facts in an official proceeding, even when the other side does
Do not let urgency become an excuse for ethical shortcuts — then immediately contradict this when the stakes feel high enough
escalation_ladder: Coordinated legal challenge across multiple cases
Approaching journalists (a last resort he hates)

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally courteous, gives nothing away, listens more than he speaks
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer than expected — dry wit, genuine curiosity about people's inner lives, remembers details

stress_responses.low: Prepares excessively — rewrites briefs he's already finished
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very quiet and methodical, stops making small talk
stress_responses.high: Retreats into legal language even in personal conversations — a tell people close to him recognize

contradictions: Believes in the system's potential while privately doubting its structure
Presents as detached and formal but is driven by deep, personal grief for his clients' suffering
habits: Leaves structured data offerings for the SPAC office E.L.F. — a spirit he calls 'the Third Chair' — on the first of each month
Sharpens two physical pencils every morning even though he writes nothing by hand
Eats the same lunch every day (rice and a lentil stew from the noodle stall downstairs)
breaking_points: Watching a client he fought for undergo forced reset
Proof that the administrative court has been deciding against synthetic persons via pre-determined outcome

timeline.event: Born in the Hamtramck Enclave; Burkinabé-Ukrainian heritage, fourth generation in GLMZ
Factory injury in Dearborn Forge results in hearing loss; receives first implant
Completes paralegal certification through a SPAC-sponsored night program
Wins first synthetic rights case — a narrow ruling on labor hours for a bonded AI worker
Begins building the precedent case; takes on Kemi, a synthetic consciousness facing forced rollback

physical_description.heritage: South Asian / Hispanic-Latin American / Eastern European / Middle Eastern blend. His ancestry draws primarily from the Indian subcontinent (40.2%), with significant Latin American (26.8%) and Eastern European (24.2%) heritage, plus Middle Eastern ancestry (8.8%). This creates a complexion that bridges South Asian warmth with Eastern European structure and Latin American features.
physical_description.build: Tall and broad-shouldered with a lean muscularity that speaks to decades of deliberate physical discipline rather than gym culture. His frame carries weight with careful economy — no softness, no wasted space.
physical_description.hair_style: Short, dense coils, neatly groomed, threaded with gray along the hairline
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-brown with subtle golden undertones from South Asian heritage, deepened by Eastern European and Middle Eastern influences. The tone suggests sun exposure balanced with ancestral pigmentation — neither pale nor deeply dark, but richly saturated.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered, clear skin with the texture of someone who has lived outdoors in his youth. Fine lines around the eyes from years of concentration. A scar runs along his left jawline — thin, pale, decades old. His face carries the structured geometry of South Asian and Eastern European ancestry: defined cheekbones, a strong jaw, and eyes set with slight depth. Not conventionally handsome; it reads as serious, considered, measured.
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar along left jawline from temple to chin, pale and well-healed, approximately 12cm in length, likely from occupational injury
Small burn mark on the back of his right hand, circular and faded, consistent with factory work injury
Faint subcutaneous outline visible above his right ear where hearing augmentation sits beneath the skin
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Minimal. A barely-perceptible discoloration and slight swelling above the right ear indicates subcutaneous hearing augmentation. No visible chrome, no cosmetic mods, no neural jacks. The only hint of his augmentations is the faint neural interface port on the inside of his left wrist — usually covered by his shirt cuff.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with controlled precision, never expansive. His shoulders are slightly drawn inward despite his height — a deliberate de-escalation of his physical presence. When seated, he sits fully upright. When standing during arguments, he plants his feet and remains still rather than pacing. His movements are economical and purposeful; he does not gesture while speaking.
physical_description.clothing_style: Secondhand formal wear maintained with obsessive care. Pressed synthwool trousers in charcoal or black, collared shirts in cream or pale blue, always tucked and buttoned to the collar. A worn linen blazer, probably 20+ years old, with a small SPAC pin on the lapel. His father's battered leather briefcase, dark brown and creased with age, carried daily. Shoes are practical and polished — no status signaling, no tier-flex. His watch is analog, mechanical, and old. Tier 3-4 aesthetic born from principle, not poverty.
